I work at the interface of quantum field: I work at the interface of quantum field theory, lattice gauge dynamics and quantum many-body physics, combining analytical model building with large-scale numerical simulation: tensor networks, Krylov methods and exact diagonalisation on Hilbert-space sectors of several million states. Developing interests span lattice QCD and gauge–gravity duality, and the translation of quantum simulation into industry-relevant technology.

The thesis investigates source-supported: The thesis investigates source-supported electric flux, matter screening and real-time response in a finite two-rishon SU(2) quantum-link model on an open honeycomb lattice, with its representation, conserved sectors and numerical accuracy specified explicitly.

On the C₂ patch, gauge-invariant sectors: On the C₂ patch, gauge-invariant sectors of up to 46,829 states (product spaces of 6.7 million) are solved exactly. A thirteen-mass ladder resolves a crossover from screening-like to confinement-like response; the heavy-mass finite-distance force is 1.03 ± 0.01 tₕ/a per link. A mass quench from m = 4 to 0.5 suppresses the source connection throughout the exact window t ≤ 20.

A Szilard-like quantum heat engine is bu: A Szilard-like quantum heat engine is built on the level degeneracy produced by inserting a barrier into a positive oscillator-shaped well. From the position-dependent energy eigenvalues, the work and efficiency of a Stirling-like cycle are computed as functions of angular frequency, well width and temperature.
How do level degeneracy, angular frequen: How do level degeneracy, angular frequency, well width and temperature determine the work and efficiency of a quantum heat engine?
Quantised spectra of semi-infinite and i: Quantised spectra of semi-infinite and infinite oscillator-shaped wells with position-dependent mass; work and efficiency of the Stirling-like cycle evaluated analytically and numerically.
The cycle delivers positive work in both: The cycle delivers positive work in both cases. In the semi-infinite well, work and efficiency depend only on the angular frequency; in the infinite well, also on its width. Both approach the classical limit at large angular frequency and the Carnot limit at low temperature.

The thesis treats non-Hermitian XY and X: The thesis treats non-Hermitian XY and XX frustrated, dimerised, quasi-one-dimensional spin chains in a transverse complex field and shows that they can be solved exactly through a fermionic mapping.
